rows.claim: Trim's seeded half builds its executor with `_scratch(sim, T, act)`
rows.evidence: src/trim.jl:603 reads `seeded_exec = _scratch(model, T).exec`; `_scratch` takes (model, T) only (src/model.jl:143-144). The activation is looked up inside `Model(deployment, T)`.
rows.fix: seeded_exec = _scratch(model, T).exec                # buffers at T, die with the call
rows.note: The other lines of the snippet match src/trim.jl:600-624 up to simplification (`_seeded` takes `Val` keys, `_establish_frozen!` takes `model.deployment.build`).

rows.claim: A bare NamedTuple handed to `linearize` gets the directive refusal `reads` gives (`ReadSetMisuse`)
rows.evidence: src/linearize.jl:282-284 refuses any non-Taps second argument as ArgumentInvalid(call=:linearize, argument=:taps, reason=:not_a_tap_set); test/test_linearize.jl:468-469; probe:D (first fail line). ReadSetMisuse comes only from `taps(...)` on a bad list (probe:D, taps(x=2.0)).
rows.fix: `taps` returns a `Taps` value holding three `Reads`, so a bare NamedTuple handed to `linearize` is refused as `ArgumentInvalid` with reason `:not_a_tap_set`, and a list that is not a NamedTuple of selectors is refused by `taps` as `ReadSetMisuse`.
rows.note: The spec (§14.10) does not name ReadSetMisuse for a bare NamedTuple at `linearize`; no spec line agrees with the companion.

rows.evidence: src/linearize.jl:512-518: the x entry the pass keeps is the pair (xbuf slot, `DerivRead{retype(T,P),C}(entry.offset)`); probe:C4 prints `(1, DerivRead{Dual{LinearizeTag,Float64,4},()}(0))` and `(2, DerivRead{...,()}(1))`. The chain parameter is `()`, not `Nothing`, and the `StateRead` is only the nominal intermediate.
rows.fix: | `x.θ` | `(1, DerivRead{Dual,()}(0))` | seed slot `xbuf[1]`, and the derivative read at `ẋbuf[1]` |   (and `(2, DerivRead{Dual,()}(1))` for `x.ω`)
rows.note: The offsets 0 and 1 are right. The prose at L403-407 (a `StateRead` bakes the `xbuf` offset) should say the resolved `x` entry pairs that site with a `DerivRead`.

rows.claim: Two taps resolving to one site are refused 'in `x`, in `u`, or one in each'
rows.evidence: src/linearize.jl:462-466 and 475-479: an `x` site is an Int (`xbuf` slot), a `u` site is a tuple (cell addr, linear index), so a key from one list never equals one from the other. probe:H: an `x` and a `u` tap in one set give no failure. test/test_linearize.jl:425-433 covers only same-list duplicates. Spec §14.10 says only 'a second tap resolving to a site already seeded'.
rows.fix: - **Two taps resolving to one site**, in `x` or in `u`: a second seed at a site would overwrite the first ...
rows.note: The spec (design/spec.md:14294-14296) does not carry 'one in each' either, so the spec and the code agree and only the companion differs.

rows.claim: The readback loop is `for (i, entry) in enumerate(x_entries)` with `_read(entry, ẋbuf_at(exec))` and a per-column `partials` loop over all columns
rows.evidence: src/linearize.jl:370-378: x entries are `(site, DerivRead)` pairs read as `_read(entry, seeded_exec)`; the partials split goes through `_readback!` (src/linearize.jl:564-571) once per group of `width` columns, inside the `Iterators.partition` loop. `ẋbuf_at` appears nowhere in src/.
rows.fix:
for (i, (_, entry)) in enumerate(x_entries)         # rows of A and B
    ẋ₀[i] = _readback!(A, B, i, _read(entry, seeded_exec), group, n_x)
end
for (i, entry) in enumerate(y_entries)              # rows of C and D
    y₀[i] = Float64(_readback!(C, D, i, _read(entry, seeded_exec), group, n_x))
end
rows.note: `_readback!` writes the group's partials into the `x` matrix for columns up to n_x and into the `u` matrix after. The snippet's two column ranges are right in effect.

rows.claim: The tests perturb one root input by 1e-6 through `about`, linearize twice and compare the difference quotient of ẋ₀ to a column of B
rows.evidence: No such test: rg '1e-6' test/test_linearize.jl is empty, and the testsets at test/test_linearize.jl:103-590 hold no finite-difference witness. probe:L1 shows the quotient (1.0000000001) matches B[:,1] = [0,1], so the check would pass.
rows.fix: Say the witness is a check one can run, not one the suite makes: '- **Finite differences as a witness.** Perturbing one root input by `1e-6` through `about` and linearizing twice gives a difference quotient of ẋ₀ that matches the corresponding column of B. The suite does not run it; ...' Or add the test.
rows.note: The sentence at L632 'Two checks the tests make' also needs the change if the bullet stays untested.
